scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r12 dummy interfaces lo1, lo2, lo3
Mechanism: r12's four /24 loopbacks live on separate Linux
  interfaces (lo, lo1, lo2, lo3) — that's the workaround for
  FRR eigrpd only advertising one prefix per interface. When
  lo1/lo2/lo3 go down, EIGRP withdraws those three prefixes;
  102.1.1.0/24 (on the real `lo`) stays advertised. R11
  withdraws them upstream into OSPF.
Localization: r12
Root cause: dummy interfaces lo1/lo2/lo3 are down on r12
Fix: `ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up`
  on r12
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up`
  on r12

line.command: ip -br link show lo1 | grep -c UP

ip -br link show lo3 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text: The three missing prefixes (102.1.2.0/24, 102.1.3.0/24, 102.1.4.0/24) are hosted on r12's dummy loopback interfaces lo1, lo2, and lo3 respectively. All three interfaces are administratively DOWN (confirmed via `ip addr show` on r12: state DOWN for lo1/lo2/lo3, while lo carrying 102.1.1.1/24 is UP). FRR's EIGRP daemon activates a `network` statement only when a matching interface is operationally up; because lo1–lo3 are down, the three corresponding /24 connected routes are never inserted into r12's EIGRP topology table. This is directly confirmed: r12's EIGRP topology shows only `102.1.1.0/24 via Connected, lo`, with no entries for 102.1.2–4.0/24. Since r12 does not originate those prefixes, r11 never receives them via EIGRP AS 100 (the EE/112.x segment), never installs them in its routing table, and never redistributes them into OSPF area 3 toward r1. The EIGRP adjacency between r12 and r11 remains fully up because the fault is on r12's loopback dummy interfaces, not the physical eth0 link — explaining why the adjacency is healthy yet the routes are absent. The root cause is that r12's startup configuration fails to bring lo1, lo2, and lo3 to an UP state before (or at the time) FRR starts. The fix is to execute `ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up` on r12 and add those commands permanently to r12's startup script so they are applied before FRR is launched.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly names r12 as the device with the down dummy loopback interfaces and root cause.
Agent explicitly identifies r12's dummy loopback interfaces lo1, lo2, and lo3 as the affected components.

The agent explicitly notes that lo1–lo3 are down while lo remains up, explains EIGRP only advertising the up interface (causing withdrawal of the three prefixes but not 102.1.1.0/24), and ties this to the observed partial route withdrawal.
Recommends running the exact ip link set lo1/lo2/lo3 up commands on r12 and persisting them, which matches the expected fix.

The logs show r12 only originates 102.1.1.0 in EIGRP and the r12 ip addr output (and frr.conf notes) indicate the other loopback/dummy interfaces are down, so the agent's inference that those down interfaces caused the missing prefixes is well supported (minor transient wording about r11's received state is inconsistent but doesn't break the core chain).
